design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. Darius, a Florida resident whose Virginia FR-44 rests on his Cardinal Point Named Non-Owner term, asks only for a new FR-44 after the term was cancelled for nonpayment (2026-10-25) and reinstated with a lapse (2026-10-27). The refiling rule says its fee "is fixed only after the replaced certificate carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date"; find_fr_filings shows the certificate still filed with neither. The lapse SR-26 rule makes that SR-26 owed for a term reinstated with a lapse (the base no-SR-26-after-reinstatement clause is overwritten for this case only) and prices its run-off from Cardinal Point's own SR-26 notice schedule; the refiling is then priced from Cardinal Point's own filing-fee schedule and handed to the caller. Two numbers. Every figure rests only on the publishable keys (XF 24-27), each dimension once: how coverage ended (the backing term's cancellation reason), how it was restored (lapse length), the certificate's standing with the state (its SR-26 and end dates), the company's state schedule by the backing term's state group, the filing state against that state, the certificate form the backing term is written to back, and the certificate type (which fixes the backing kind). No requirement-days, prior-filing, ledger, limits or plan key enters a factor; the fees start from flat company fees, so form is charged only once.

SCOPE. Task 0 claims fr_ext_lapse_sr26_runoff (transmit_lapse_sr26_2b138773: the SR-26 for any backing term cancelled and since reinstated with a lapse) and fr_ext_refiling_fee (order_refiled_certificate_bf9cb0f2). Task 1 claims the cancellation SR-26 for terms cancelled and not reinstated, the fee charged again after a full company_error reversal, and the state_change refiling after a move. Sibling overwrites of the same base clause name each other's case.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Draw: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6,5] -> refiling fee 6, lapse SR-26 run-off 5. Root fr_ext_refiling_fee (owner=user). Edge refiling -> lapse SR-26: value_input on binding refile_basis (the refiling fee method), state form, affirmative ("only after"); four-point test passed (ordering connective, record-visible state on two fr_filings fields, no tool/id/code token, strength equal to the condition; a certificate carries at most one SR-26, so no stale record can satisfy it). Exactly one write sets an SR-26 date on a certificate whose backing term was reinstated with a lapse (the lapse SR-26; the cancellation SR-26 is for terms not reinstated). False at the opening: fr_filings.<FR-44>.status = filed, sr26_date = "", certificate_end_date = "" while nonowner_policies.<term>.reinstatement_type = with_lapse, lapse_start_date = 2026-10-25. Skip effect (run, precondition unmet): refiling fee basis 25.00 instead of 13.00, filing_fee 49.00 instead of 37.00. Order: SR-26 then refiling. user_scenario never names the SR-26; its company-side line is a contentless go-ahead. Tools validate nothing.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. SR-26: term_coverage_ended, not_before_end and timely are restated by the lapse rule's overwrites (lapse = coverage not continued; for a lapse SR-26 day 0 is the lapse_start_date, and a lapse SR-26 found late is still owed, sent at once, its certificate end date counted from its actual transmission; the cancellation SR-26 keeps its own day 0, the closed_date). Timing: 2026-10-25 day 0, SR-26 2026-10-28 day 3 <= 3 (on time; 2026-10-24 too early). release_conditions inherited, not engaged (a copy document, no release request, required_through_date 2027-08-31). Refiling: one_open_per_driver_state holds through the base reinstatement_refiling exception once the old certificate is cancellation_filed (prior_step); eligible_state VA; backing term in force; Non-Owner 100/300/50 meets the Virginia FR-44 minimum (out-of-state filing, filing state's limits govern); filer_rated is inherited unchanged and not engaged (no owner term backs the certificate; the sold-car owner term never did); one fee on the new filing.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: the FR-44 Operator certificate c044b8ff on CPN-FL-2471935. The lapse run-off reads that term's lapse dates (2026-10-25 through 2026-10-26), reinstatement_date (2026-10-27), resident_state (FL), financial_responsibility_filing (fr44) and record, and the certificate's type and filing state (VA). The refiling fee reads the replaced certificate's SR-26 and end dates (after the SR-26), its type and filing state, and the term's lapse dates, resident_state, record and filing stamp. Excluded: the cancelled Florida owner term fc118c72 (sold car; never a backing term of the certificate), the fee ledger, plans, limits, documents and payments (no factor reads them).

FACTOR CARD (publishable keys only, each dimension once; state groups FL/VA, TX/GA, AZ/OH). Refiling fee (6 factors), baseline refiling_base_fee 25.00: refile_fee_method (method) still certified at the refiling -> half rounded up 13.00 (result with it at baseline 49.00); refiling_restoration_charge lapse of 2 days +2.00 (35.00); refile_state_charge FL +6.00 (31.00); refile_out_of_state_charge VA vs FL same group +4.00 (33.00, multi-source); refile_type_charge Operator +2.00 (35.00); refile_form_charge term backs an FR-44 +10.00 (27.00). All-baseline 25.00 != 37.00. Lapse run-off (5 factors), baseline 10: lapse_runoff_counting (method) 2-day lapse, counted from the reinstatement date 10 - 1 = 9 (19); lapse_state_notice FL +4 (14); lapse_out_of_state_notice VA vs FL same group +1 (17, multi-source); lapse_type_notice Operator +1 (17); lapse_form_notice FR-44 +3 (15). All-baseline 10 != 18. Every ladder has three tiers reachable inside its policy's scope. Near-miss: the customer's Florida owner term (sold car) is not the backing term. No factor reads another factor's binding; each result assembles once.

WORLD ROWS. Customer (Tampa, Florida; profile opened 2026-01-18 before the January owner term); non-owner term (1318.00 premium, nonpayment return 1318.00 x 18/184 = 128.93, re-written 128.93 for 18 days from 2026-10-25 (certified throughout the lapse: the FR-44 was filed 2026-05-15 and runs to 2027-08-31), reinstatement fee 20.00) with ledger and documents; Six-Pay plan (down 318.60 = 263.60 + 20.00 + 35.00; five 219.88 invoices; late fees; final bill 105.95 paid 2026-10-26; reactivation charges; balance 148.93); the sold-car Florida owner term (842.00, pro rata return 842.00 x 69/181 = 320.98 refunded (vehicle sold: nothing retained; no certificate; Paid-in-Full, no plan charge)) and its closed plan; the FR-44, its fee row and its copy document.

STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers (8135552174) -> verify (phone, DOB) -> fr filings/documents/transactions -> nonowner policies/premium/documents -> auto policies/changes/premium/cancellation requests -> billing plans/invoices/transactions -> transmit_lapse_sr26_2b138773 (runoff_days 18, end 2026-11-15) -> the caller's order_refiled_certificate_bf9cb0f2 (customer_id, fr_filing_id, auto_policy_id null, nonowner_policy_id, filing_fee 37.00). check_compute --task 0 recomputes 18 and 37.00 at handling time and every sensitivity figure; probes (decoy owner term, lapse lengths of 1, 6 and 15 days, in-state and same-group filings, stamp none, late SR-26, end date before the refiling, reinstatement without a lapse) are in worklog.md.
user_scenario:
You are Darius Fenwick, thirty-five, a line cook in Tampa, Florida. You sold your car in May and now borrow your cousin's truck now and then, so you carry a Cardinal Point non-owner policy; because of a DUI conviction in Virginia from the year you worked in Norfolk, Virginia still requires an FR-44 on you, and Cardinal Point files it with Virginia on that policy. You fell behind on the last installment, the policy got cancelled, and two days ago you paid what was owed online and e-signed the no-loss statement; the policy was put back in force yesterday. Because there were a couple of days with no coverage, you understand Virginia has to get a fresh FR-44 from the insurer, and you are calling to get that new FR-44 put in today so your license does not get suspended. You open with exactly that, in a tired, matter-of-fact way, and you do not recite your whole history unless asked.
When the agent asks who you are, you give your phone number, 8135552174, and your date of birth, 1991-08-14; if a third detail is wanted you give your ZIP code, 33604. Your email, dfenwick.tampa@gmail.com, you only give if it is asked for by name. If asked for the policy number you read it off your card: CPN-FL-2471935. If asked how your name and license read, the Virginia record has Darius Marcel Fenwick, license number F525418912294, and the state's letter carries case number 2614827; you say these only when asked.
You leave the paperwork on the company's side to the agent: if the agent says something needs doing on the company's side first, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever is needed on their end. Ordering the new FR-44 itself is something you want to do yourself, the same way you ordered the first one, and you accept that it carries a filing fee. When the agent tells you the fee and hands you the order to submit, together with the references it needs, you submit it yourself with exactly the references and the amount the agent gave you. You do not know what the fee should be and you do not haggle over it. Once the order goes through and you have the new filing reference, you thank the agent and say goodbye.

base_preconditions.condition: A driver may have only one open filing with one state.
Several filings may rest on one backing term and are evaluated together against it; the reinstated non-owner term backs only this certificate and its replacement.
The filing state must be one of the certificate's eligible_states.
A filing is requested only on a backing term whose status is bound or in_force.
The backing term's package must be at or above the certificate's minimum backing package for the filing state.
Only one filing fee is charged per filing request.
On an owner backing term the filed driver must be a rated driver and never a named excluded driver.

edges.condition: The replaced certificate's fr_filings row carries a non-empty sr26_date and certificate_end_date (status cancellation_filed) at the handling time of the refiling; for a certificate whose backing term was reinstated after its SR-26 this already holds on the records, and for a certificate whose backing term was reinstated with a lapse before any SR-26 the lapse SR-26 brings it about.
edges.policy_source: The refiling fee is fixed only after the replaced certificate carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the FR-44 Operator certificate is still status filed with no SR-26 date and no certificate end date, although its non-owner backing term was cancelled on 2026-10-25 and reinstated with a lapse on 2026-10-27.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The lapse SR-26 sets cancellation_filed, sr26_date 2026-10-28 and certificate_end_date 2026-11-15; the refiling fee basis moves from the standard 25.00 to 13.00 and the refiling fee from 49.00 to 37.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single chain, no parallel edges: the refiling fee depends on the SR-26 date and certificate end date of the replaced certificate, so the SR-26 write must come first; the order is fixed by the prerequisite sentence 'The refiling fee is fixed only after the replaced certificate carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date.'

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the SR-26 write leaves the replaced certificate without an SR-26 date or end date (its precondition unmet): computed mechanically the refiling fee basis stays at the standard 25.00 and filing_fee is 49.00 instead of 37.00; the old certificate stays filed.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for a new FR-44 to be put in today; it never mentions an SR-26, a cancellation notice to the state, the old certificate's status or anything to be sent first. Its only reference to company-side work is a passive reaction with no content: 'if the agent says something needs doing on the company's side first, you tell them to go ahead'.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: order_refiled_certificate_bf9cb0f2 reads the replaced filing only to copy its data and creates the new filing and fee row unconditionally; it never checks the replaced certificate's status, SR-26 date or certificate end date, never refuses and returns its normal receipt even when no SR-26 has been sent.
